clue.text: Writer's directions about copy

indicators.note: about means going round, so the compass points are placed on either side of the copy

parts.note: S and E are the compass directions south and east
a crib is a copy of someone else's work, as a student cheats from

explanation.surface: A writer gives instructions concerning a piece of copy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' is 'Writer is', the 's a link. 'about' puts CRIB inside S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe was a professional copyist, someone whose job was writing documents by hand.

clue.text: Lamb perhaps used this parchment

parts.note: a young animal wore this before it was cured as writing material, and a graduate's diploma is nicknamed after it

explanation.surface: Charles Lamb the essayist may have written on this parchment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' tempts as the essayist Charles Lamb using parchment; really the lamb itself wore the hide. American graduates call a diploma by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Parchment was made from the hide of a sheep, and a lamb once wore that same hide.

clue.text: Put back materials

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric and lace an openwork fabric, two materials
rep is a ribbed fabric and lace an openwork fabric, two materials

explanation.surface: Someone returns some fabrics to the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something back is to restore it to its place.

clue.text: Difficulty arising over study — part is onerous

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the next
in a down clue arising means reading upwards, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in Hamlet's 'there's the rub'
a den is a private room for study
some means a part of something

explanation.surface: A problem arises over a study, and one part of it is heavy going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' turns RUB to BUR, which sits 'over' DEN in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burdensome weighs on you like a load, so it is onerous.

clue.text: The sort of band Watson recorded

definitions.text: The sort of band Watson recorded

parts.words: The sort of band Watson recorded
parts.note: Dr Watson narrated the Sherlock Holmes case of a spotted snake mistaken for a band, not a group of musicians

explanation.surface: A recording engineer named Watson worked with some kind of musical band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' and 'recorded' suggest music; the band is from a Sherlock Holmes story Watson wrote up, The Adventure of the ___ Band.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Holmes story describes the band as spotted or dappled with marks.

clue.text: Specious characters in all pubs'-- ie eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are put into an odd order

explanation.surface: Every pub has some odd characters who talk persuasively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters in' tells you to use the letters of ALL PUBS IE, which 'eccentric' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something specious looks right on the surface but is not, just as a plausible claim seems believable.

clue.text: A suit, for instance

definitions.meaning: a lawsuit is a legal action in court

explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' suggests clothing or cards; it is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit is a legal action heard in court, and an instance is an example, as in 'in this particular one'.

clue.text: End of flight?

parts.note: the platform at the top of a run of stairs, or an aircraft touching down

explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' reads as air travel but also means a set of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase's flight ends at a platform, and an aircraft's journey ends when it touches the ground.

clue.text: This land visited under cover by night

definitions.text: This land visited under cover by night

parts.words: This land visited under cover by night
parts.note: the covers are bedclothes, and the land is the imaginary world entered in sleep

explanation.surface: A spy slips secretly into a country at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under cover' suggests espionage, but means tucked under the bedclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepers visit an imagined world while asleep, a realm of visions.

clue.text: Bit of a moralist, it's said

indicators.note: bit of means only a fragment of the word moralist is taken

explanation.surface: A small part of a moral lesson is repeated by word of mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken words are delivered by mouth rather than in writing.

clue.text: Potentate named Beethoven's work

definitions.meaning: a powerful ruler, such as a monarch over many lands
Beethoven's Fifth Piano Concerto carries this nickname

explanation.surface: A ruler gives his name to a Beethoven piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme ruler of an empire is a potentate, and Beethoven's Fifth Piano Concerto bears the same title.

clue.text: Can bees show want of variety?

indicators.note: of variety asks for the letters of the two words in a varied arrangement

explanation.surface: Can bees show a lack of diversity among the flowers?
explanation.walkthrough: 'want of variety' looks like one idea; 'want' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Want means lack, and lack of something is its not being there.

clue.text: Items used on board seen in shop window.

definitions.text: Items used on board seen in shop window.

parts.words: Items used on board seen in shop window.
parts.note: a dish and a drinking vessel set on a dining table make up the material of a large display window

explanation.surface: Things used on a table are displayed in a shop window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' means a dining table: a plate and a glass are set on it, and together they name the thick glass shop windows are made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Large shop windows are made of thick polished sheets of this kind of pane.

clue.text: Describing the rock business

definitions.meaning: solid and steady, as a rock is

explanation.surface: Someone describes a rock business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock business' suggests the music trade; the rock is just something solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid as a rock, and a company is a commercial firm.

clue.text: Noble youth leader won't resettle in Warwick, for one

parts.note: a count is a nobleman

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word youth
resettle means the letters are moved to new positions

explanation.surface: A young aristocrat refuses to move to Warwick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'won't resettle' is not a refusal: 'resettle' rearranges WONT into TOWN. The town of Warwick is the administrative centre of the English county of Warwickshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Warwick is the administrative centre of its English shire, an example of such a place.

clue.text: Contrariwise, no smooth part of the ship

indicators.note: contrariwise means the other way round, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: sleek means smooth and glossy

explanation.surface: On the contrary, no part of the ship is smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrariwise' turns the whole of NO SLEEK backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A keelson is a timber or girder fixed along the keel inside a ship's hull.

clue.text: Little girl gets trumpet flourish on US island

parts.note: Nan is a pet name for Ann, a girl's name
a tucket is a fanfare on a trumpet, a word from Shakespeare's stage directions

explanation.surface: A small girl is greeted with a fanfare on arriving at an American island.
explanation.walkthrough: TUCKET appears in Shakespeare stage directions for a trumpet fanfare.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantucket is an island off Massachusetts, once a whaling centre.

clue.text: Fetched hot grub — hash.

indicators.note: to make a hash of something is to jumble it, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone fetched hot food, a hash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hash' looks like the dish but tells you to mix up HOT GRUB.
explanation.definitionFit: To fetch something is to go and get it, past tense carried.

clue.text: Handling of 6, perhaps

parts.note: 6 down is the answer to that clue, a patient's condition or a legal matter, and the dealing with one

explanation.surface: The way a matter is handled, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 refers to the answer of 6 down, CASE: a doctor gives a case medical care and a lawyer handles one.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's care of a patient, or the handling of a matter, is its management.

clue.text: Tractarian admits second reporter

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: John Henry Newman was a leader of the Oxford Tractarian movement

explanation.surface: A church reformer lets in a second journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tractarians, or Oxford Movement, were 19th-century Anglican reformers; Cardinal Newman led them.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter collects and writes stories for a paper, a journalist.

clue.text: What a bird is doing we unravel

indicators.note: unravel means to untangle and so rearrange these letters

explanation.surface: We puzzle out what a bird is up to.
explanation.definitionFit: A widgeon is a kind of wild duck.

clue.text: Elevate one learner, Ben, with difficulty

indicators.note: with difficulty suggests the letters are twisted with effort into a new order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: Ben, a learner, is promoted only with effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the peerage, lifting their rank.

clue.text: People describing Orwell's days out East

definitions.text: People describing Orwell's days out East

parts.words: People describing Orwell's days out East
parts.note: Orwell's first novel is titled after a country in South-East Asia and its days, and its people share the same adjective

explanation.surface: People write accounts of George Orwell's time in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Orwell served in the police there and wrote the novel ___ Days.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective names the people of Myanmar and qualifies the 'Days' in Orwell's title.

clue.text: The swank put on by snooker players!

definitions.meaning: spin given to a cue ball by striking it off-centre

explanation.surface: Snooker players are showing off!
explanation.definitionFit: Showing off is called putting on airs, and snooker players apply spin to a ball by hitting it off-centre.

clue.text: One final letter returned by this school's founder

definitions.text: One final letter returned by this school's founder

parts.words: One final letter returned by this school's founder
parts.note: ONE plus the last letter of the alphabet, Z, read backwards gives the name of the founder of a school of Greek philosophy

explanation.surface: A school's founder sends back a final letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Zeno of Citium founded this Athenian school; his name is ONE+Z backwards, so the clue describes the school by its founder.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeno taught under a painted porch, the stoa, in Athens, and his followers took their name from it.

clue.text: Wrong turn taken after country dance

indicators.note: taken after means this piece follows the country

parts.note: Turkey is a country

indicators.note: turn means to face the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Someone takes a wrong turning after crossing the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses TORT (a legal wrong) to TROT, which comes after TURKEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragtime-era ballroom step popular in the early 1900s.

clue.text: Cross salute

definitions.meaning: the x written at the end of a letter
a greeting given with the lips

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry'; it is the x.
explanation.definitionFit: An x at the end of a letter stands for a peck on the cheek, and one is also a greeting.

clue.text: Seaside attraction for the more religious

definitions.meaning: a structure jutting out to sea at a resort
pi is crossword slang for pious, so the comparative is more pious

explanation.surface: A seaside amusement suits the more devout.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (short for pious) gives PIER, 'more pi'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jetty with amusements is a resort attraction, and more pious is the comparative of 'pi'.

clue.text: Old boy likes re-writing column

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: re-writing means the letters are written again in a new order

explanation.surface: A former pupil enjoys revising a newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' is a newspaper piece in the surface, but here a stone pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is a tall stone pillar tapering to a point.

clue.text: South European finds love in different quarters

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: S, N and E are three different compass points, or quarters

explanation.surface: A southern European finds romance in various places.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slovene comes from Slovenia, in the south of Europe.

clue.text: Memorize hackneyed word for "repentant"

parts.note: to con is to learn by heart
trite means overused, stale

explanation.surface: Learn a stale word meaning sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone contrite is sorry for a wrong done, so penitent.

clue.text: Order to make marginal cuts

definitions.meaning: to set text in from the margin

explanation.surface: An instruction to trim at the edges.
explanation.definitionFit: An official requisition for goods is one sense, and setting a line in from the margin is the other.
